card.title: Houston Plant Manager
card.description:
Axalta has remained at the forefront of the coatings industry by continually investing in innovative solutions. We engineer technologies that protect customers’ products – whether they are battling heat, light, corrosion, abrasion, moisture, or chemicals – and add dimension and beauty with colourful finishes. We have a vast and ever-evolving portfolio of brands primed to play an important part in everything from modernizing infrastructure around the world to enabling the next generation of electric and autonomous vehicles.

We are currently looking for a **Plant Manager** to join us at our facility in **Houston, TX.**

**Position Description:**

The Plant Manager will develop and execute the manufacturing strategy to meet Axalta’s business requirements; drive process excellence in every step of the manufacturing process; implement improvements to reduce the cost of goods sold (COGS); and, direct Plant Management, including Quality, Engineering and EH&S. The Plant Manager will lead actions for all operations at Houston.

The Plant Manager is responsible for analyzing local plant requirements and working cross-functionally within operations (internal manufacturing, external manufacturing, supply chain, procurement) as well with functions outside operations (businesses, HR, Finance, Legal). The successful candidate will leverage knowledge of industry best practices and financial analysis/modeling to recommend solutions to enhance operations performance and profitability. The position will translate Regional and Global operations strategy into local execution while developing and ensuring consistent and efficient flow of product and supply chain from supplier to customer, as well as enabling best-in-class service to internal and external customers.

The qualified candidate will be a high-energy self-starter with a strong work ethic who must excel at both day-to-day tactical execution as well as long-term strategic planning. This individual must be motivated by a competitive industry and be an expert at fulfilling customer requirements and maximizing profitability. Excellent communication and leadership skills, as well as deep, relevant experience across multiple functions/facets of a best-in class manufacturing organization(s), will be critical to success in this role.

**Responsibilities:**

* Responsible for all plant operations and facilities at site.
* Direct line responsibility for nine (9) direct reports and employees and over 100+ indirect reports.
* Full accountability for all aspects of an integrated coatings facility including production, warehousing, maintenance, process engineering, quality control, and safety.
* Full accountability for all local site regulatory matters.
* Inculcate a continuous improvement mindset that drives improvements in quality, cost, delivery, and inventory every day
* Provide strong leadership to Manufacturing, Quality, EH&S and Engineering, and build capabilities around these areas.
* Manage operations budget through continuous productivity improvement and quality control.
* Bring operational excellence and discipline to the site and execute AOE strategy.
* Be data driven yet able to implement solutions at an appropriately urgent pace.
* Must have demonstrated ability to communicate effectively with cross functional stakeholders and various levels of employees.
* Strong financial and analytical skills; must be able to develop and implement a strategy to maximize productivity and profitability.
* Strong chemical batch processing knowledge in a lean environment with high customization amongst products, including experience applying or implementing lean manufacturing, kaizen methodology and productions systems.
* Demonstrated experience in gathering and reporting business data and key performance indicators.
* Able to adeptly operate in a matrixed reporting structure.
* Create and manage operational and capital budgets.

**Qualifications:** 
Incumbent must be able to perform each duty satisfactorily and in a safe and manner. The items listed below represent the knowledge, skills, and experience required.

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry or related discipline required. Advanced degree desired.
* Minimum 10 years manufacturing experience, including years in the chemicals or related industry (coatings experience strongly preferred), as well as at least 10 years leading managers highly desired.
* Knowledge on non union sites.
* Knowledge and experience managing a site Process Safety Management (PSM).
* Must be able to work flexible hours and/or overtime when needed.
* Work requires manual dexterity, accuracy and attention to detail.
* Heavy visual and mental concentration and periods of prolonged sitting are required.
* Occasionally required to conduct production floor and warehouse visits requiring prolonged standing or walking, negotiation of obstacles, and bending or stooping.
* Strong communication and influence skills required; must be able to effectively enact change management and implement and lead new initiatives and programs.

Axalta operates its business in two segments: Performance Coatings and Mobility Coatings, which serve four end markets, including Refinish, Industrial, Light Vehicle and Commercial Vehicle, across North America, EMEA, Latin America and Asia-Pacific. Our diverse global footprint allows us to deliver solutions in over 140+ countries and coat 30 million vehicles per year. We’ve recently set an exciting 2040 carbon neutrality goal, in addition to 10 other sustainability initiatives, and we take pride in working with our customers to optimize their businesses and achieve their goals.

The expected compensation range for this position is $180,000 - $200,000 USD annually.

Axalta has remained at the forefront of the coatings industry by continually investing in innovative solutions. We engineer technologies that protect customers’ products – whether they are battling heat, light, corrosion, abrasion, moisture, or chemicals – and add dimension and beauty with colorful finishes. We have a vast and ever-evolving portfolio of brands primed to play an important part in everything from modernizing infrastructure around the world to enabling the next generation of electric and autonomous vehicles.

Axalta operates its business in two segments: Performance Coatings and Mobility Coatings, which serve four end markets, including Refinish, Industrial, Light Vehicle and Commercial Vehicle, across North America, EMEA, Latin America and Asia-Pacific. Our diverse global footprint allows us to deliver solutions in over 140+ countries and coat 30 million vehicles per year. We’ve recently set an exciting 2040 carbon neutrality goal, in addition to 10 other sustainability initiatives, and we take pride in working with our customers to optimize their businesses and achieve their goals.

Axalta may use technology-assisted tools, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support certain aspects of the recruitment and selection process. These tools may be used to help manage applications, identify job-related qualifications, and assist recruiter review. All hiring decisions involve human oversight and review.

We consider an individual’s qualifications, skillset, and experience to determine final salary. This role is eligible for benefits such as health insurance and paid time off. The actual offer will be at the company’s sole discretion and determined by relevant business considerations, including the final candidate’s qualifications, years of experience, skillset, and geographic location.

card.title: Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations Engines - BE-4
card.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

You will join a skilled team responsible for rocket engine production serving customers. Reporting directly to the Engines VP, you will oversee an Engine Production group. The Sr Director leads Senior Managers, whose teams manage daily rocket engine production at Huntsville. This hands-on, influential role calls for outstanding leadership, strong communication, careful judgment, knowledge of mid-rate production, and solid project management expertise. This job will play a vital role in space exploration history and demands your dedication and meticulous focus on safe, repeatable spaceflight.

**Responsibilities include but are not limited:**

* Coordinate activities related to factory design, equipment identification, equipment procurement, production readiness, production start-up, and transition into low-rate initial production.
* Collaborate with the leadership group at our current (Kent, WA) site to grasp existing production processes and convert these strengths into the new manufacturing facility.
* Collaborate with the Huntsville Site Leader and Engines Program Management for communications and support involving both internal and external customers.
* Champion and lead improvement teams for manufacturing processes, business processes, production planning, and implement lessons learned and other standards/processes as needed.
* Manage the Production capital project portfolio and ensure timely execution of projects to support corporate Annual Operating Plans.
* Participate in the preventive action process and implement plans as required.
* Communicate and enforce mission assurance and safety principles throughout the organization.
* Find opportunities for safety improvements, cost savings, and other means to accelerate progress.
* Coordinate and complete site level initiatives with other members of the Huntsville Senior Leadership Team.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Minimum of a B.S. degree or equivalent experience in Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering. M.S. is preferred and MBA or equivalent experience is a plus.
* 15+ years’ experience in aerospace or a closely related industry, such as launch vehicles, aircraft, helicopters, excavation/heavy hauling, mining, energy, or shipbuilding.
* Experience managing customer relations and expectations.
* Prior experience managing Profit and Loss at a program or project level.
* Proven ability in project coordination, budget oversight, and guiding teams.
* Experience leading and managing small- to medium-sized teams on fast-paced projects.
* Technical expertise in managing medium rate production activities.
* Experience in process definition, development, deployment, and improvement.
* Strong quality outlook with special attention to safety and critically important quality aspects as well as application of root cause analysis tools.
* Strong personnel management and mentoring skills.
* Strong safety approach and experience, including hands-on experience planning and conducting critical operations.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing or Toyota Production System. Six Sigma Black Belt certification preferred.
* Experience simultaneously managing activities in multiple departments or sites.
* Experience transitioning products from development to production.
* Knowledge of fabrication processes, integration processes, systems engineering practices, test, quality, and configuration management systems.
* Experience managing facility level capital improvements.
* Experience with new process development.
* Experience in staffing and launching a new production facility.

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
Location(s):
Fort Smith, AR, US, 72916

Function: Manufacturing

Audience: Experienced Professional

Work Arrangement: On Site

Requisition ID: 71047

**PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

The Fort Smith **Plant Leader** has overall responsibility for the entire manufacturing facility, and oversees the development and implementation of organizational strategies, standards, and practices to achieve best-in-class performance. In addition, the Plant Leader collaborates closely with other Plant Leaders and leadership across the business to drive success of the enterprise. The Plant Leader is also an active member of the community and represents Owens Corning’s interest in local affairs.

 

Fort Smith is part of Owens Corning’s North America Nonwovens business and manufactures Nonwovens products. Fort Smith’s primary customers are in the building materials market (Wet Formed Mat). This position has 7 salaried direct report and 1 dotted-line report. The Plant has 160 employees.

 

**Reports to:** Global Operations Director, Nonwovens

**Span of control:** Operations Leader (Coating Line), Operations Leader (Wet Formed Mat Line), TPM Leader, Maintenance Leader, Quality/Technical Leader, EHS Leader, Plant Controller, HR Leader (Dotted-Line)

 

**Benefits of Working at Owens Corning:**

* 72 Consecutive years as a Fortune 500® Company

* The Wall Street Journal Best-Managed Companies Top 250

* $10.1 Billion in 2025 Sales Revenue
* Presence in 31 Countries with 25,000 employees

* Health and Wellness Opportunities
* Adoption and Family Assistance- OC is committed to helping employees in their endeavor to build a family, including financial assistance for adoption and surrogacy
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) provides U.S. employees the opportunity to purchase Owens Corning stock at a 15 percent discount every six month
* Parental leave- Four weeks of paid time off for all new parents; this includes both mothers and fathers at the time of birth or the adoption of a child
* A rebate program that allows employees to receive a rebate of up to $2,000 every four years for purchases of OC’s wide range of products for new construction or home improvement

Just what is it that makes Owens Corning unique? Of course, there are the products, the global reach, and the strong commitment to sustainability. Behind all of that though, it is our people and our purpose. That is our difference. We are proud to be recognized for our ongoing product, environmental and social sustainability efforts:

* Placed on the Dow Jones Sustainability World Index (DJSI World) for the 15th consecutive year (2024)
* Ranked in the top 10 of the 100 Best Corporate Citizens List for the 8th consecutive year (2025), No. 3 overall
* Recognized by the Ethisphere Institute as one of the 2023 World’s Most Ethical Companies - Sixth Consecutive Year

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

**Responsibilities:**

**Lead safety and security for an injury free work environment**

* Ensures a culture which enables a safe and secure work environment for all employees, contractors, and visitors
* Shows passion and caring for our people, and leads from a place of “safety and” the other objectives of the business with a focus on safe behaviors and choices
* Allocates resources and identifies investments required to achieve zero injuries, including systems, focused programs, and leadership
* Ensures a clear and effective measurement system is followed and used to drive results; rewards and celebrates safe behavior and achievements; ensures accountability
 

**Lead the facility through a Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) operating system targeting**

* Zero injuries
* Zero defects
* Zero losses
 

**Know the business and our customers**

* Continuously build insight into the business’s market, customer base and strategies
* Create an environment where all employees are engaged, empowered, and focused on serving our customers
* Develop relationships with customers and understand what it takes to ensure OC products are perceived by the market as high quality.
* Models this customer first mindset and consistently applies quality systems and standards to drive out quality issues.
 

**Execute business strategy and direct operations that drive towards manufacturing excellence**

* Leads with a clear view of where the organization needs to be in 1-3 years
* Communicates strategic direction to employees and how it fits with the day-to-day actions and results being driven. Ability to achieve results through the team. Effective utilization of 2-way communication tools to share strategy and target objectives.
* Set clear and measurable performance expectations, in line with division and corporate goals; proactively analyzes and manages all relative operations performance metrics
* Oversee the development of a comprehensive annual capital budget and operations plan; initiates timely and appropriate capital requests to maintain or enhance plant performance necessary to meet customer demands
* Operate with zero environmental non-conformities to applicable company, government, and regulatory policies
* Continuously improves the plant operations environmental footprint consistent with company goals and community interests
* Ensures appropriate resources to business strategy and deliverables.
* Demonstrated change agent who can lead strategic transformation.
 

**Develop a positive employee relations environment**

* Ensures a positive, creative, diverse, and collaborative work environment where employees own the success of the business.
* Selects, trains, ensures the proper tools processes and systems are in place, then empowers employees to deliver against clear expectations.
* Monitors labor activities to ensure compliance with company policies and/or governmental regulations
* Establishes OC as an employer of choice in the local market
* Builds a facility worthy of use as a marketing and communications platform, both internal and external
* Maintains effective relationships with key political and community decision makers and represents the Company in appropriate community matters
 

**Lead and develop talent**

* Create an environment where talent is developed, and full potential is realized.
* Effectively build a diverse team with competent people using the appropriate mix of internal promotions and external recruitment to satisfy near-term performance, longer-term succession needs and to ensure the organization has the necessary talent to achieve its near-term and long-term goals.
* Ensures alignment with functional leadership (e.g., finance, safety, human resources) on performance management and talent development
 

**Lead across the network manufacturing facilities and integrated supply chain of the business**

* Leverage partnership with other leaders across the integrated supply chain to maximize performance of the business, lead change, and grow talent
* Share best practices, challenge thinking and provide candid and respectful feedback; set an example for the organization of how teamwork and partnerships should work
* Be seen as a great leader across the business, driving engagement and supporting cross-functional projects and teams.
 

**Job Requirements:**

 

**Education:**

* Master’s Degree preferred, Bachelor’s Degree required with preference on engineering, business or related majors will be considered
 

**Experience:**

* Engineering or technical background preferred
* At least 5 years of experience in a Plant operations leadership role managing salaried employees
* 10+ years of experience in various manufacturing roles
* Exposure to cross-functional team leadership or participation outside of manufacturing
* A history of hiring, growing, and promoting talent within the organization
 

Type of Industry

* TPM formal training, or strong background in Continuous Improvement, and Lean manufacturing, experience
* Experience successfully designing and leading culture change within an organization
* Experience meeting customer demands.
* Paper and pulp, automotive, electronics, bulk industries
 

**Knowledge and Skills:**

* Act as an organizational steward
* Collaborates and fosters teamwork
* Develops people
* Competitively drives results
* Follows through on commitments
* Allocates necessary resources
* Actively listens
* Thinks and acts strategically
* Models’ curiosity and growth mindset
* Challenges the status quo
* Generates ideas through diverse thought
* Works from an outside in perspective
* Effective with verbal and written communication
* Business and financial acumen
* Mindset of creating value for the customer
 

**Travel**

* Must be able to travel up to 10%
 

*This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee(s) incumbent in this position. Employee(s) will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by any person authorized to give instructions or assignments.*
 
*A review of this position has excluded the marginal functions of the position that are incidental to the performance of fundamental job duties. All duties and responsibilities are essential job functions and requirements and are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities. To perform this job successfully, the incumbents(s) will possess the skills, aptitudes, and abilities to perform each duty proficiently. Some requirements may exclude individuals who pose a direct threat or significant risk to the health or safety of themselves or others. The requirements listed in this document are the minimum levels of knowledge, skills, and abilities.* 
*This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an “at will” relationship.*

card.title: Director of Continuous Improvement
card.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

In this role, you will guide enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen operational performance, enhance quality, and increase efficiency across multiple manufacturing sites. You will lead efforts that reduce waste, improve process capability, and support teams in optimizing complex aerospace and defense production workflows, helping ensure mission-critical hardware is delivered with consistent excellence.

#### **Duties/Responsibilities**

* Develops and deploys a multi-site continuous improvement roadmap aligned with corporate objectives.
* Leads lean, six sigma, and value stream mapping initiatives to drive operational excellence.
* Identifies and eliminates non value added activities across machining, fabrication, and downstream processing.
* Develops, tracks, and reports enterprise metrics for cost savings, yield improvements, and cycle time reduction.
* Partners with manufacturing engineering, quality, and supply chain to improve process capabilities.
* Facilitates advanced root cause problem solving activities to address systemic production bottlenecks.
* Plans and executes kaizen events focused on setup reduction, 5S workplace organization, and cellular manufacturing.
* Mentors and develops employees in lean and six sigma methodologies.
* Ensures continuous improvement initiatives support and maintain AS9100 and product safety standards.

#### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, or a related technical field.
* Minimum 8-10 years of operations or continuous improvement leadership in aerospace and defense manufacturing.
* Certified lean six sigma master black belt or black belt.
* Experience with AS9100 quality management systems and defense contract management agency (DCMA) oversight.
* Background in precision machining, structural fabrication, or aerospace assemblies.
* Proficiency with enterprise resource planning (ERP) and manufacturing execution system (MES) data analysis.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Master of business administration (MBA) or master's degree.

#### **Special Mentions**

* Travel is required across regional manufacturing sites.

#### **Benefits**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health savings account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible spending accounts (FSA)
* Company-paid life and AD&D insurance
* Short- and long-term disability coverage
* Tuition reimbursement

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
**Make a SPLASH with Latham, The Pool Company!**
================================================

At Latham, The Pool Company, we don't just make swimming pools; we create opportunities for backyard dreams to come true. As the leading manufacturer in North America, Australia, and New Zealand, we are committed to delivering innovation, quality, and sustainability in everything we do.

We believe in building an environment where everyone can thrive. That is why we offer:

* A culture of integrity, collaboration, and respect.
* Comprehensive benefits for you and your family.
* Opportunities for growth, mentorship, and skill development.

**A little about the position:**

**Job Summary:**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, and continuous improvement of an Automatic Pool Covers manufacturing facility. This role directs all aspects of plant operations, including production, safety, quality, inventory management, workforce development, maintenance, and cost control. The Plant Manager ensures customer orders are fulfilled on time, within quality standards, and in a cost-effective manner while fostering a culture of safety, teamwork, accountability, engagement, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

***Please note this position is located in Plainfield, Indiana. You would need to be able to commute or willing to relocate to the area.***

 

**Some of What You Will Do:**

* Provide visible leadership that promotes a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
* Lead, coach, and develop supervisors, managers, and frontline employees.
* Build organizational capability through succession planning, talent development, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Champion a zero-incident safety culture and ensure compliance with all OSHA, environmental, and company requirements.
* Ensure effective implementation of safety programs, training, incident investigations, and corrective actions.
* Direct daily operations of custom automatic pool cover manufacturing, assembly, and shipment activities.
* Ensure production schedules are achieved while meeting safety, quality, delivery, and cost expectations.
* Optimize labor utilization, production efficiency, and manufacturing throughput.
* Ensure products meet customer specifications and company quality standards.
* Drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions to improve first-pass yield and reduce warranty claims.
* Maintain appropriate inventory levels while minimizing excess and obsolete inventory.
* Partner with Planning, Purchasing, and Supply Chain teams to ensure material availability and inventory accuracy.
* Drive lean and value engineering initiatives with support from corporate team to drive continuous improvement and gross margin improvement.
* Utilize data, KPIs, and visual management tools to drive decision-making.
* Develop and manage annual operating budgets and forecasts.
* Identify and implement cost-saving opportunities while maintaining quality and service levels.

**What You Bring to the Table: (Qualifications)**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, Industrial Technology, or related field preferred.
* Minimum 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years of plant management or operations leadership experience.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt preferred.
* Strong leadership, teambuilding, people management skills.
* Demonstrated understanding of safety, quality, productivity, inventory management, and employee relations.
* Proven experience developing and implementing processes that drive continuous improvement.
* Proficiency in reading and interpreting business reports, metrics, and KPIs.

**Why Join Latham?** **At Latham, we invest in your well-being, growth, and success. Our comprehensive benefits package supports you and your family with:**

* Medical, dental, and vision coverage
* 24/7 telehealth and wellness resources
* Personalized benefits advocacy and support
* Expert second opinions and access to leading specialists
* 401(k) with a 50% company match up to 6%, and financial protection benefits
* Flexible PTO and 11 paid holidays
* Mental health, family care, and financial wellness resources

**Join a team that's invested in your well-being, your future, and your success.**

**Some Important Information for you:**

**Position Title:** Plant Manager

**Location:** Plainfield, Indiana

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Status:** Exempt

**Salary Range:** $100,000 - $146,000

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across US geographic markets. Starting pay for this role will vary based on multiple factors, including location, knowledge, skills, education, and experience. Pay ranges may be modified in the future.

**Bonus:**MIB Tier 2 - 17.5%

 

*Latham, The Pool Company is an* ***Equal Opportunity Employer****. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status. Latham, The Pool Company is a Drug-Free Workplace Employer. All offers of employment are subject to applicable pre-employment requirements.*

Owns the assigned plant, including the plant’s operating budget, and leads production activities for assigned manufacturing facilities and/or value streams with direct accountability for safety, quality, cost, schedule attainment, and on-time delivery. Provides site-level leadership to ensure daily execution aligns with production plans, customer requirements, standard work, and business objectives. Partners cross functionally with Planning, Materials, Engineering, Quality, HR, and Manufacturing leadership to remove constraints, improve process discipline, and drive continuous improvement throughout the operation.

**Minimum Qualifications: (Education, Experience, Knowledge, and Skills):**

* Bachelor’s degree with 3–5 years of supervisory or site leadership experience and 5–7 years of manufacturing experience preferred. In lieu of a degree, a high school diploma/GED with a minimum of 8 years of supervisory or relevant manufacturing leadership experience will be considered.
* Demonstrated ability to lead a manufacturing site, department, or value stream with accountability for safety, quality, schedule, cost, labor planning, and daily execution.
* Experience leading production managers or production teams through daily management routines, KPI reviews, structured escalation, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong understanding of production scheduling, capacity planning, labor utilization, material readiness, ERP/MRP discipline, and schedule attainment in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated competency with ERP systems used in manufacturing environments; IFS, SAP, Oracle, or similar systems preferred.
* Working knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, 5S, visual management, standard work, root cause problem solving, and Corrective Action/Preventive Action practices; Six Sigma and/or Lean certification preferred or actively pursuing.
* Ability to use operational data, reports, and KPIs to communicate performance versus goals and drive improvement in safety, quality, cost, schedule, productivity, and on-time delivery.
* Knowledge of safe work practices, OSHA requirements, incident prevention, corrective action closure, and operational organization standards.

card.title: Plant Manager
card.description:
Select Milk Producers is one of the nation’s largest and most progressive dairy cooperatives, with 32 wholly owned subsidiaries, 8 processing plants, and 8 joint ventures including Continental Dairy Facilities, Continental Dairy Facilities Southwest, Mill Haven Foods, Select Custom Solutions, GreenLink and Select Services. With over 800 employees, the Select Milk family of companies impacts all aspects of the dairy farm business and at the heart of our family of companies, is you.

"We strive to go above and beyond what’s expected in providing for our families, leading our employees, caring for our land and animals, serving our customers, producing quality milk, and serving one another. This commitment is more than our business, it’s in our culture and our character. We believe in being accountable, in doing what’s right, in performing at our best, in setting a higher standard."

Select Milk Producers and its subsidiaries offer an attractive compensation and a best-in-class benefits package that includes but is not limited medical, vision, dental, life insurance and more that can be tailored for you and your family. Other benefits for eligible employees include 401(k) up to 6% company match, life and disability insurance, and paid holidays & vacation. We are proud to promote an equal employment opportunity workplace.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Plant Operations: Review daily inventories and plan daily production. Conduct daily staff meetings to coordinate daily plant activities. Review daily load out schedule and coordinate with staff and milk movement personnel. Review daily production efficiencies and production reports. Review companies KPI’s, plant loss and assist in setting goals. Reports directly to the Director of Operations.
* Plant Quality: Review microbiology test results daily and direct further investigation of high counts. Review list of any out-of-spec. product with Food Safety Quality Assurance (FSQA) Manager. Review all product C of A's.
* Plant Audits: Check each department daily. Check employee GMP’s. Review daily report of audits. Assist Quality Assurance with all plant audits.
* Industrial Wastewater: Check wastewater facility daily. Review daily reports as required.
* Sanitation: Review CIP records daily. Review random equipment checks with chemical account representative.
* Plant Employees: Audit sampling techniques and sanitation practices. Monitor production departments throughout shift and assure employee compliance with GMP’s, sanitation and safety. Provide training as needed. Provide annual GMP and HACCP training.
* Purchasing: Review and approve order supplies. Track purchases and prepare appropriate paperwork.
* Equipment: Verify that all plant equipment is in good working condition and all preventative maintenance is being performed on a scheduled basis. Review and approve all work orders. Review all daily maintenance activity reports. Develop capital justifications to update equipment as needed.
* Environmental: Review of Air Quality annual reports. Review and coordinate completion of Annual Form R for EPA/Health Department. Review and coordinate completion of Annual Hazardous Materials Inventory and Business Plan. Perform other duties, as necessary.
* Safety: Review Safety program and training with EHS management. Daily observation during plant audit will include safety. Check each department and observe employee safety procedures. Member of the Food Safety Team and Food Quality Team.
* Leadership: Utilize Code of Conduct and core values to drive development and growth opportunities for all team members.
* Support a company culture of continuous improvement by participating in efficiency and improvement efforts.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**:

* This position has management and employee supervisory responsibilities for the entire facility in the area of discipline, hiring, and firing.
* Review on the job training reviews.
* Coordinate on the job training.
* Oversee adherence to company policies and procedures.
* Oversee scheduling of management, employees, and temporary labor.
* Have the responsibility of reviewing timesheets, overtime and approve payroll.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES REQUIRED:**

* An individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
* Must have the ability to trouble shoot problems and be persistent until a solution is found.
* Must work in a safe manner and follow all safety procedures including use of safety equipment.
* Must be willing to ask for assistance when the process is unclear.
* Proficient in verbal and written communication skills. Must be able to communicate with upper management on a daily basis.
* Leadership, team development, coaching, and / or teaching experience.
* Good math and statistical skills.
* Excellent computer skills for data input, report writing, program tracking.
* Excellent organizational and follow through skills.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Dairy or Food Science and four years of experience in a Plant leadership role in a Dairy or Food Manufacturing facility is strongly desired.

card.title: Director of Manufacturing
card.description:
**Company Overview:**

Adams Communication & Engineering Technology (ACET), Incorporated is a Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) system engineering and information technology firm. Incorporated in 1999, we support mission critical Information Technology (IT) business needs for clients within the intelligence community (IC), Department of Defense (DOD), Veteran Administration (VA) and for select commercial clients. ACET, Inc.’s technical, programmatic, and analytical professionals are experts in commercial technology, customized solutions, and proprietary government systems.

**The Position:**

ACET is seeking an experienced, results-driven **Director of Manufacturing** to lead all production, fabrication, assembly, and shop-floor operations at our **Havelock, NC** facility. Reporting directly to executive leadership, the Director of Manufacturing will oversee day-to-day plant performance, drive operational excellence, ensure strict adherence to DoD quality and safety standards, and partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, and Program Management to deliver defense projects on time and within budget.

**Responsibilities:**

* Direct all daily manufacturing, machining, fabrication, and assembly operations in Havelock to meet customer delivery schedules, cost targets, and quality specifications.
* Partner with Program Managers and Engineering teams to transition designs from rapid prototyping and Engineering Manufacturing Development (EMD) into Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) and full-rate sustainment.
* Enforce compliance with ISO 9001, AS9100, and Department of Defense manufacturing standards, ensuring zero-defect delivery and full audit readiness.
* Lead, mentor, and schedule production supervisors, machinists, technicians, and quality personnel; foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and high retention.
* Implement Lean, Six Sigma, and 5S methodologies to optimize shop-floor workflow, reduce cycle times, minimize scrap, and control overhead rates.
* Collaborate with Procurement and Contracts to manage long-lead materials, vendor bottlenecks, equipment maintenance, and capital expenditure planning.
* Maintain a safe, OSHA-compliant manufacturing environment while upholding all DoD physical security and classified material handling protocols.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related technical field (or equivalent military/industry leadership experience).
* Minimum of 8–10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including at least 3–5 years in a Plant Manager, Manufacturing Manager, or Director-level role within the aerospace, defense, or government contracting sector.
* Proven expertise in precision machining, sheet metal fabrication, electro-mechanical assembly, ERP/MRP systems, and reading complex engineering drawings/blueprints.
* Hands-on experience operating under ISO 9001 and/or AS9100 quality management systems.
* U.S. Citizenship required; must hold an active DoD Secret security clearance (or have the ability to obtain and maintain one).

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Prior experience supporting NAVAIR, Fleet Readiness Center East (FRC East), or USMC/DoD aviation sustainment programs.
* Certification in Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma (Green Belt or Black Belt).
* Experience managing manufacturing operations within a small-to-midsize defense contractor environment, including familiarity with FAR/DFARS compliance and government-furnished property (GFP).

**Why Join ACET:**

ACET continues to expand its aerospace and aviation sustainment operations supporting multiple Department of Defense aviation platforms worldwide. This position provides the opportunity to directly shape strategic sustainment growth initiatives while supporting operational readiness and mission success across the global aviation enterprise.

**What We Offer:**

At ACET, we believe that our employees are our most valuable asset. We are committed to providing a comprehensive Total Rewards program that recognizes and supports the diverse needs of our workforce. Our offerings are designed to attract, motivate, and retain top talent while fostering a culture of excellence, innovation, and well-being.

Employee benefits include the following:

* Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage
* Life insurance, AD&D, and Short- and Long-Term Disability
* 401(k) Program
* Wellness programs
* Paid Time Off
* 11 Paid Holidays
* Employee Referral Program
* Employee Assistance Program

*Please note that all compensation, benefits, and policies are subject to change at the company's discretion. While we make every effort to provide advance notice of changes, adjustments may occur based on business needs, economic conditions, and industry standards.*

**\*\*Must be US Citizen to apply\*\***

The above job description is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of duties and standards of the position.

**Drug Free Workplace:**

ACET is a Drug Free Workplace where post offer applicants and employees are subject to testing for marijuana, cocaine, opioids, amphetamines, PCP, and alcohol when criteria are met as outlined in our policies.

**ACET is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action Employer and VEVRAA Federal Contractor**.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

card.title: Plant Director
card.description:
**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!**
Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you'll lead great people, drive meaningful impact, and help shape the future of our business while supporting the bakery and restaurant teams behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests enjoy every day. That's the kind of culture that has earned us a place on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For® list every year since 2014.

**The Plant Director**
provides strategic and operational leadership for a three-shift, seven-day manufacturing facility encompassing approximately 160 full-time, non-union employees. Leading all aspects of production and packaging operations, you will drive performance, efficiency, quality, and continuous improvement across scheduling, logistics, pre-scaling, mixing, depositing, baking, decorating, and packaging to support the Bakery's operational and business objectives.

They utilize excellent leadership, analytical, management, and technical skills, abilities, and behaviors to drive performance in key areas such as people, safety, quality, service, and cost, aligned with measurable objectives and the Company’s Mission, Vision, and Values. The Director also assists with business continuity in the absence of the VP of Operations.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **Service oriented:**
 you are a people person who is systematic and trustworthy and interacts constructively with peers or teams of various levels demonstrating strong, positive communication skills.
* **Driven by results:**
 you are conscientious and persistent about delivering timely, high-quality deliverables, and performing all job functions safely while following instructions.
* **Improvement focused:**
 you never turn off the thought “how can I do this better/faster”.
* **Pressure resistant:**
 you have ice in your veins while under pressure. Maintaining a positive outlook at work while the heat is on is never an issue for you.

**Here’s more of what you’ll get to do:**

* Maintain positive employee relations through respectful, open, and effective two-way communication at the individual and team levels.
* Partner with human resources and training departments to develop, implement, and maintain effective training and development programs that support performance goals and provide a satisfying work environment.
* Maintain a fair and professional work environment that balances business objectives with quality-of-work-life factors for employees.
* Work with Human Resources to ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and company policies, while driving improvements in employee performance as measured by turnover rate, attendance, and feedback mechanisms.
* Oversee production planning and scheduling to optimize service and efficiency, balancing resources such as crewing, materials, and equipment with other department managers.
* Supervise the development of synchronized crewing, equipment setup, and materials preparation plans to ensure schedule attainment and optimize capacity utilization.
* Manage timekeeping, labor efficiency, and plant productivity in compliance with legal and company policies, aiming to minimize overtime and control non-productive line time.
* Collaborate with the Plant Engineer to ensure preventive and emergency maintenance efforts are effective, minimizing downtime and optimizing machine performance.
* Manage material usage to ensure minimal waste and maximum yield, while maintaining strict adherence to product quality standards and inventory management.
* Monitor spending and manage operations within approved budget levels, while driving improvements in cost performance through labor productivity, waste reduction, and yield maximization.
* Ensure disciplined compliance with product and process quality standards, food safety, and regulatory requirements, striving for “EXCELLENT” or “SUPERIOR” scores in third-party audits.
* Lead plant safety efforts, including co-chairing the Safety Steering Committee, safety inspections, and training, while driving improvements in safety performance as measured by injury frequency and workers' compensation data.
* Participate in business plan development, budgeting processes, and plant-level meetings to ensure effective communication and alignment with operational goals.
* Ability to transform the facility into a CI culture driven by people, process and equipment/technology.
* Ensure the utilization of 4-step process to drive result in sustainability which are Huddles, Daily meeting, utilization of Red Zone and Sic meetings.

**What we require:**

* Minimum of 15 years of experience in food manufacturing management, preferably in the bakery/dessert industry, with demonstrated success at the Plant Manager or Director of Manufacturing/Operations level.
* Bachelor’s degree (MBA a Plus)
* Strong experience with food safety, food process equipment, and regulations.
* Strong experience with emergency preparedness and emergency response plans and procedures.
* Familiar with regulatory and safety codes, including USDA, FDA, and OSHA regulations.
* Knowledge and demonstrated skill in lean manufacturing, Kaizen, kitting, and Six Sigma techniques.
* Prior experience with direct responsibility for a large-scale P&L.
* Strong and effective strategic management skills, including long-range planning, organizing, communicating, influencing, gathering and using information, and motivating a team to achieve results. Ability to use, and teach others to use, various analytical tools and techniques.
* Demonstrated mentoring skills.

**What we offer:**

* Eligible for annual bonus
* Eligible for annual equity grants
* Medical, Dental & Vision
* Eligible for benefits first day of the month following date of hire
* 401K with company match
* 3 weeks of vacation which increases to 4 weeks starting in your 5th year
* 5 days of sick time per year (first year prorated)
* Tuition Reimbursement of $2,500 for qualified programs
* Adoption Assistance Benefit of $2,500
* 25%-35% discount when dining as a guest
* Reusable gift card loaded annually for your dining enjoyment

**About the Company:**

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery creates over 35,000 delicious cheesecakes per day across our two facilities in Calabasas, CA and Rocky Mount, NC plus other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees, and third-party bakery customers.

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery is a subsidiary of The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated. Recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® since 2014, The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a global $3.8 billion public company with more than 370 casual dining restaurants and over 48,000 staff members.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming workplace for all. We welcome applicants from a wide variety of identities, ideas, perspectives, backgrounds and experiences to apply. The Cheesecake Factory offers reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities.

#SoCheesecake #LifeAtCheesecake

To notify of a non-compliant job posting, please send a notice to ats@thecheesecakefactory.com.

card.description:
**Director of Operations & Production**

**Location:**
Redwood City, CA

**Schedule:**
Full-time, onsite

**Industry:**
Precision Manufacturing

**About the Company**

An established precision component solutions provider with a significant manufacturing operation in Redwood City is seeking a Director of Operations & Production. The company serves leading customers across the medical, aerospace, and electronics industries and operates within an ISO 9001/AS9100-certified quality management environment.

The organization is committed to delivering high-quality products, strong customer service, and operational excellence. They believe successful business outcomes begin with strong employees, clear processes, and a culture of accountability.

**About the Role**

The Director of Operations & Production will oversee day-to-day operations and help drive efficiency, productivity, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the business. This person will manage and support multiple departments, including purchasing, shipping, customer service, production planning, inventory, and operational processes.

The ideal candidate will have a strong manufacturing operations background, sharp business judgment, and experience managing cross-functional teams in a time-sensitive production environment. This role requires someone who can work closely with production leaders, customers, vendors, and internal teams to ensure operational goals are met and company processes run smoothly.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Oversee daily operations across purchasing, shipping, customer service, production planning, inventory, and related operational functions.
* Maintain consistent communication with customers, managers, staff, and vendors to ensure smooth company operations.
* Lead, motivate, and support teams within a fast-paced and demanding manufacturing environment.
* Partner closely with production department managers on scheduling, production execution, technical problem-solving, resource planning, and priorities.
* Develop and oversee production control processes for raw materials and shop floor production.
* Track and respond to changing customer requirements related to pricing, delivery, and production timelines.
* Support quoting activities by providing operational input for new and existing products.
* Develop, implement, and maintain quality management system protocols within operational processes.
* Improve existing processes and procedures to increase internal capacity, productivity, and efficiency.
* Ensure operational activities remain on time and within budget.
* Track staffing needs and support hiring as needed.
* Develop career development plans for direct reports and support team problem resolution.
* Manage data collection and reporting for productivity targets, cost reduction, error reduction, and customer service improvement.
* Work closely with facilities and safety teams to ensure compliance.
* Oversee raw materials and inventory accuracy.

**Qualifications**

* 2+ years of proven success in an operations management or director-level role.
* Experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably related to precision components, metal parts production, aerospace, medical, electronics, or similar industries.
* Strong ability to delegate responsibilities while maintaining operational control and accountability.
* Experience managing production planning, customer service, purchasing, shipping, inventory, or related operational teams.
* Knowledge of ERP systems used for production planning, work order processing, and material planning.
* Strong understanding of process improvement, operational metrics, and productivity tracking.
* Experience with human resources practices, employee relations, and employment law.
* Strong conflict management and business negotiation skills.
* Excellent communication, leadership, and problem-solving abilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in operations management, engineering, business administration, or a related field.
* Working knowledge of ERP systems for small to mid-sized manufacturing businesses.
* Strong IT skills and ability to work with outside managed service providers to support business needs.
* Experience with cost accounting and reporting in a manufacturing environment.

**Work Environment**

This is an onsite role based in Redwood City, CA. The role is primarily office-based with regular interaction on the manufacturing shop floor, including collaboration with production staff and occasional machine or part inspection.

card.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
card.description:
Domino’s Pizza, which began in 1960 as a single store location in Ypsilanti, MI, has had a lot to celebrate lately: we’re a reshaped, reenergized brand of honesty, transparency and accountability – not to mention, great food! In the rise to becoming a true technology leader, the brand is now consistently one of the top five companies in online transactions and 65% of our sales in the U.S. are taken through digital channels. The brand continues to ‘deliver the dream’ to local business owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores. That’s just the tip of the iceberg…or as we might say, one “slice” of the pie! If this sounds like a brand you’d like to be a part of, consider joining our team!
 
 
**Job Description**
The Director, Continuous Improvement leads the Supply Chain-wide capability for identifying, prioritizing, enabling, and sustaining improvements that increase business performance and organizational effectiveness across functions and end-to-end processes. This role establishes a culture of continuous improvement, advances operational and business process excellence, and enables measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, service, and capacity.
 
 
Working closely with cross-functional Supply Chain leaders, this position standardizes processes, uses data and insights to prioritize opportunities, and implements sustainable solutions aligned with strategic objectives. The Director maintains a strong connection to frontline operations by working directly in Supply Chain Centers and other functional environments to understand processes firsthand and translate observations into meaningful improvements.
 
 
**What You’ll Do**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive Continuous Improvement strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with Supply Chain priorities, and advise Supply Chain leadership on opportunities that improve productivity, efficiency, cost, service, quality, capacity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Lead the deployment of consistent Continuous Improvement methodologies, tools, governance, performance expectations, and resource prioritization across Supply Chain functions.
* Work directly with Supply Chain Centers and functional teams to observe work at the point of execution, identify process variation and non-value-added activities, and implement standardized processes, operating practices, management systems, standard work, and process controls.
* Lead cross-functional transformation and productivity initiatives, including process redesign, technology-enabled improvement, automation, and new ways of working, in partnership with functional leaders, the PMO, Finance, and other stakeholders.
* Establish measurable outcomes, baselines, KPI definitions, reporting standards, dashboards, and processes for tracking, validating, and sustaining financial benefits, productivity improvements, and business value.
* Build organizational Continuous Improvement capability through training, coaching, structured problem-solving, knowledge sharing, and the development of CI team members and functional leaders.
* Lead change management and cross-functional alignment, manage risks and barriers, strengthen process integration, and communicate priorities, progress, results, and recommendations to Supply Chain leadership and key stakeholders.

**What You’ll Bring**
In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:
 
 
Be Curious
 
 

* Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
* Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots
 
 

* Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
* Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High
 
 

* Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
* Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast
 
 

* Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
* Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More
 
 

* Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
* Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations
 
 

* Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino’s Ways of Working.
* Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
* Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
* Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline; an advanced degree or MBA is preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, business transformation, operational excellence, or related disciplines, including demonstrated leadership experience in complex, cross-functional organizations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing Continuous Improvement strategies and delivering measurable business results across multiple functions or complex organizations.
* Strong knowledge and practical application of Lean Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, process optimization, standardization, and change management methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change without direct authority.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience leading Continuous Improvement initiatives in manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or other complex operational environments, including the ability to engage frontline employees, site leaders, and senior executives to diagnose issues, implement solutions, and deliver measurable results.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience identifying, quantifying, and validating productivity improvements, cost savings, and business value.
* Well-developed team building and influencing skills, unquestioned integrity, and the experience and confidence to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
* Experience developing performance management frameworks, leveraging data analytics, and translating insights into actionable business recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to build organizational capability through coaching, talent development, and deployment of Continuous Improvement methodologies.
* Strong strategic thinking, communication, collaboration, and executive presentation skills.
* Experience managing complex improvement portfolios, prioritizing competing business needs, and delivering sustainable outcomes.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated Continuous Improvement expertise is preferred.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including Canada, as business needs require. Expected travel is up to 50%

**Additional Information**
Benefits:
 
 

* Paid Holidays and Vacation
* Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
* No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
* Childcare tuition discounts
* No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
* Fertility benefits
* Adoption assistance
* 401k matching contributions
* 15% off the purchase price of stock
* Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

card.description:

**Salary: $90,000 - $100,000**

**Position Summary:**
The Plant Manager is a dynamic and people-focused leader responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations of the plant while fostering a culture rooted in human-centered leadership. This role emphasizes managing people with empathy and authenticity, celebrating their successes, and cultivating an environment of inclusion and belonging. The RSO Plant Manager is committed to growing and developing a high-performing team while driving operational excellence. Key responsibilities include managing plant operations ensuring the plant is compliant with all safety policies and procedures, driving continuous improvement, and championing Rehrig’s mission and values.

**Key Accountabilities:**

1. **Demonstrate and Ensure Human-Centered Leadership:**
 * Lead with empathy and understanding, prioritizing the well-being and development of all team members.
 * Recognize and celebrate individual and team achievements to foster a positive and motivating work environment.
 * Promote and maintain a workplace culture where all employees feel valued, included, and empowered to contribute.
 * Implement and execute the plant’s People Engagement plan
2. **Ensure Compliance with Environmental, Health, Safety & Sustainability (EHS&S):**
 * Perform frequent compliance reviews. Lock out tag out (LOTO) periodic inspections, site safety checklist, EHS&S calendar action items.
 * Perform frequent Behavior Based Safety Observations (BBSOs)
 * Perform frequent 5S inspections to ensure facility is compliant.
 * Monitor Site EHS&S Scorecard and utilize Velocity EHS to identify leading indicators.
3. **Drive Continuous Improvement:**
 * Build continuous improvement activities into the daily work at the plant by involving the team in Kaizen activity. Utilize Kaizen methodology along with other tools such as Plan Do Check Act (PDCA) and A3 to drive continuous improvement.
 * Monitor KPI Metrics to drive decision-making
 * Develop and help manage capital improvement projects
 * Manage and support site CI tracker to analyze efficacy of CI projects
4. **Maintain Operational Excellence:**
 * Oversee plant operations to ensure high standards of Quality and Productivity are consistently met to standard.
 * Operate within Site budget by managing plant resources effectively

**Qualifications:**

* Experienced in plant management or a similar leadership role for at least 3 years.
* High School diploma required or equivalent.
* Experience in driving continuous improvement initiatives.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Commitment to team development and operational excellence.
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under pressure.

Why Rehrig Pacific?

Rehrig Pacific is a leading manufacturer of integrated sustainable solutions for the supply chain and environmental waste industries with a diverse customer list of industry leaders. We provide end-to-end solutions including returnable plastic products, delivery lifts and sleds, technology to track those assets, and a service team to ensure their longevity. Our team is dedicated to the values, mission, and unique culture within our organization that celebrates our people. We believe in fostering an environment where employees can be their authentic selves and know that they are viewed as integral members of the Rehrig Pacific Family.

Rehrig Pacific Company is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. See also here.

card.title: Director Advanced Manufacturing
card.description:
About the company

We're an EV commercial vehicle manufacturer based in Orange County, California. We design and build our medium-duty electric vehicles in-house, and next year's production is already fully sold out.

* 1,000+ vehicles built so far
* A 2,000-vehicle order from one of the largest US parcel carriers, due by end of 2027
* $650M+ raised, including a $200M+ Series recently
* Growing beyond trucks into energy storage, autonomy and defense

The role

We've sold out of trucks, and we don't want it to happen again. We're hiring a
**Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering**
to grow our production capacity and own how we get there.

You'll lead the team that designs, buys and launches our new lines and equipment. Your decisions will show up directly in how many trucks leave the factory each month.

What you'll do

* Lead and grow the advanced manufacturing engineering team
* Own the manufacturing strategy and capital plan for scaling production
* Take new lines and equipment from concept through design, build, install, testing and start of production
* Plan capacity so production keeps ahead of customer demand
* Run equipment and facility projects to budget and schedule, and present them to the executive team
* Work closely with vehicle engineering, supply chain and operations so new designs can be built at volume
* Bring in integrators and equipment suppliers, and manage them through delivery

What you'll bring

**Must have**

* 8+ years in manufacturing engineering, with 4+ years leading teams
* A track record of growing production capacity: new lines, factory expansions or ramping to full rate
* Hands-on experience taking equipment from specification through install, testing and launch
* Experience building and managing capital budgets
